newsitem.title: UK: CFTC not discouraged by Sumitomo copper statements.
newsitem.headline: CFTC not discouraged by Sumitomo copper statements.

text.p: U.S. financial regulator the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) said it was not discouraged by recent announcements by Sumitomo Corp regarding the copper trading scandal, a CFTC official said.
Early last week Sumitomo announced it had found no evidence that its former chief copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka manipulated the world copper market.
The company also said it had found no evidence yet to lead it to take formal legal action against foreign metal brokers.
Some copper industry sources suggested the annoucements could be a setback to overseas regulatory bodies conducting their own investigation into the copper market.
But CFTC Commissioner Joseph Dial told Reuters on Monday that this was not the case.

"We're proceeding with our investigation in co-operation with the SIB (UK regulator Securities and Investments Board) and Japanese authorities," Dial told Reuters on the fringes of a conference on risk management in agriculture.
"We don't view their annoucement (Sumitomo's) as a setback...(or) discouraging. The scope of the investigation is much larger than that," he added.
He would not give an estimate of how long it would take for the CFTC's investigation into the copper market to be completed, but suggested it would be some time.

"There is a tremendous amount of paperwork the regulatory agencies have to go through, and they will be very meticulous," he said. "It is going to take a considerable time period before any announcements are made," he added.

Dial said he had been in London for a week and had taken the opportunity to make contact with the SIB and the SFA (Securities and Futures Authority), the London Metal Exchange (LME) and the London International Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE).
He also made contact with financial institutions including Goldman Sachs, BZW, the investment banking arm of Barclays plc, and Union Bank of Switzerland.
"But I did not come (to the UK) for the purpose of talking about Sumitomo," Dial said.
Dial said the CFTC and other regulators has invited financial regulators to meet in London in November to discuss futures contracts which provide for physical delivery.
"This is an outgrowth of the need to improve co-operation and communication between those regulators that have oversight of physical delivery futures contracts," he said.
He added that the conference would look into whether there is the will "to move forward in dialogue that would consider approporiate minimum regaultory standards for the world".
